issues.failure_explanation: Every characteristic-based object in the paper (the CODE maps, \(\widetilde\Omega(t)\), \(\widehat\Omega\) in \eqref{eq-HatOmega}, the upstream cells \(\widetilde\Omega^{n+1,n}_{\mathcal K}\) in the scheme) presupposes that solutions of \(\dot{\mathbf{x}}=\mathbf{A}(\mathbf{x},t)\) starting in the bounded domain exist on all of \([0,T]\) and map bounded sets to bounded sets. Under the stated assumption (\(\mathbf{A}\) merely C^1 in \(\mathbf{x}\) and t) this fails: with d=1, A(x,t)=x^2, x(t)=x_0/(1-x_0 t) blows up at t=1/x_0. Since a C^1 field has unique ODE trajectories, characteristics never intersect, so the paper's only restriction T<T* is vacuous (T*=\(\infty\)) and the paper explicitly claims no upper limit on T; yet for A=x^2, \(\Omega=(1,2)\), T\(\ge\)1 the CODE maps and \(\widehat\Omega\) are not defined on the whole domain, a periodic extension \(\widehat U\) of a nonzero U is then not in L^2(\(\widehat\Omega\)), and the theorems' quantifier 'for any time partition T=N\(\Delta\)t' is unsupported.

failure_location.quote: Let \(U \in L^2(\Omega)\). Extend \(U\) to \(\widehat{\Omega}\) under periodic boundary conditions or compact support constraints to obtain \(\widehat{U}\), where \(\widehat{\Omega}\) is defined as in \eqref{eq-HatOmega}. Then, \(\widehat{U} \in L^2(\widehat{\Omega})\).

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add a standard standing hypothesis guaranteeing global existence of characteristics on [0,T] (e.g., \(\mathbf{A}\) bounded or of at most linear growth in \(\mathbf{x}\), uniform in t), or restrict T to the flow's maximal existence interval; then \(\widehat\Omega\) is bounded, the extension result holds, and all stated theorems survive unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: Without a global-existence assumption, the constructions underlying the whole paper (CODE, \(\widetilde\Omega^{n+1,n}_{\mathcal K}\), \(\widehat\Omega\), the discrete scheme \eqref{eq-discrete-SLDG}) are ill-defined in an advertised regime, and the well-posedness theorems quantifying over arbitrary T are unsupported.
issues.title: Missing global characteristic-existence hypothesis (blow-up not excluded by T<T*)
issues.why_classification: Adding a standard global-existence/linear-growth condition is a local hypothesis fix: the method, all conclusions, the stability constant's stated dependencies, and the demonstrated scope (all four numerical tests satisfy it) survive intact.

issues.failure_explanation: Both set inclusions in the proof are argued via the false equivalence x in supp(f) iff f(x)!=0: the support is the closure of the nonvanishing set, so a support point can be a zero of f (e.g., \(\Psi(x)=x\) on (-1,1) has 0 in supp(\(\Psi\)) but \(\Psi(0)=0\)). Hence neither bullet proves its stated inclusion as written. The lemma's conclusion is nevertheless correct, because \(\psi(\cdot,t^*)=\Psi\circ\Phi\) with the flow map \(\Phi\) a homeomorphism implies supp(\(\psi(\cdot,t^*)\))=\(\Phi^{-1}\)(supp(\(\Psi\))).

issues.why_classification: The conclusion is correct and the repair is a routine, local support-chasing argument; no statement and no downstream result changes.

issues.failure_explanation: The premise is false for P>2: compactly supported L^2 functions need not lie in L^P for P>2 (e.g., d=1, \(\Psi(x)=(x-1)^{-1/3}\chi_{(1,2)}(x)\) lies in H_0((0,3)) but is not in L^4(\(\mathbb{R}\))). The proof therefore does not support the lemma's norm-invariance claim for P>2 from the stated H_0(\(\Omega\)) hypothesis; only 1\(\le\)P\(\le\)2 is legitimately covered (on bounded support L^2 embeds in L^P for P\(\le\)2).

failure_location.quote: Given that \(\Psi(\mathbf{x}) \in H_{0}(\Omega)\), it follows that \(\Psi \in L^P(\mathbb{R}^d)\) for \(1 \leq P < \infty\).

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Assume \(\Psi\in L^P(\mathbb{R}^d)\) directly, or restrict the statement to 1\(\le\)P\(\le\)2; no further change is needed for this defect beyond the separate Jacobian correction of ISSUE-004.
issues.overall_effect: The P>2 portion of the lemma's claim is unsupported; the lemma is auxiliary and only the P=2 case is ever used downstream (via Lemma lemma-psi-Omega-LP), so no other result is affected by this defect.
issues.title: False premise that H_0(Omega) is contained in L^P(R^d) for all 1<=P<infinity
issues.why_classification: A local hypothesis/quantifier repair on an auxiliary lemma whose P>2 case is never used; every substantive claim survives unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Note that once \(t_1\) and \(t_2\) are fixed, \(\int_{t_1}^{t_2} \mathbf{A}(\mathbf{s}(\tau), \tau) \, \mathrm{d}\tau\) is a constant.

issues.failure_explanation: The substitution x = x* + \(\int_{t_1}^{t_2}\mathbf{A}(\mathbf{s}(\tau),\tau)d\tau\) is the characteristic flow map \(\Phi\), not a translation: \(\mathbf{s}\) depends on x* through \(\mathbf{s}(t_1)=\mathbf{x}^*\). The claim that this displacement has zero x*-derivative, hence dx = dx*, is false: by Liouville's formula det(D\(\Phi\)) = exp(\(\int_{t_1}^{t_2}\nabla\cdot\mathbf{A}\,d\tau\)), which equals 1 only for divergence-free fields, an assumption the paper never makes for the general problem \eqref{eq-scalar-linear-transport}. Concrete counterexample: d=1, A(x,t)=x, \(\Psi\in L^2(\mathbb{R})\) gives \(\psi(x,t_1)=\Psi(e^{t_2-t_1}x)\), so \(\|\psi(\cdot,t_1)\|_{L^2(\mathbb{R})}=e^{-(t_2-t_1)/2}\|\Psi\|_{L^2(\mathbb{R})}\neq\|\Psi\|_{L^2(\mathbb{R})}\). Both invariance lemmas are therefore false as stated; the boundedness step of Lemma Lemma-f-H* and the key equality \(\|\psi^0\|_{L^2(\widetilde\Omega^{1,0}_{\mathcal K})}=\|\Psi^{(\mathcal K)}\|_{L^2(\Omega_{\mathcal K})}\) in the stability and uniqueness proofs inherit the error, although the existence, stability (with a modified constant still depending only on (T, \(\Delta\)t, \(\Omega\), \(\mathbf{A}\))), and uniqueness conclusions survive once a bounded Jacobian factor is carried through.

failure_location.quote: Considering the \(L^P\)-norm over the entire space \(\mathbb{R}^d\), the domain of integration remains unchanged as \(\mathbb{R}^d\) before and after the change of variables. Thus, we immediately obtain

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the false identities by the standard estimate \(\|\psi(\cdot,t_1)\|_{L^P(\widetilde\Omega^{t_1})}\le(\sup\det D\Phi^{-1})^{1/P}\|\Psi\|_{L^P(\widetilde\Omega^{t_2})}\) with det(D\(\Phi\))=exp(\(\int\nabla\cdot\mathbf{A}\)), and propagate the bounded factor through Lemma-f-H* and the stability induction (per-step factor \(e^{C\Delta t}\), global factor \(e^{CT}\), so the stability constant still depends only on (T, \(\Delta\)t, \(\Omega\), \(\mathbf{A}\))); alternatively add the hypothesis \(\nabla\cdot\mathbf{A}=0\), which all four numerical tests satisfy but which narrows the stated generality.
issues.overall_effect: The two L^P-invariance lemmas fail at the paper's stated generality (arbitrary C^1 velocity field); the boundedness argument in Lemma-f-H* and the per-step norm identities in the stability and uniqueness proofs are invalid as written, so those proofs go through only after the false equalities are replaced by Jacobian-weighted estimates.
issues.title: Characteristic change of variables treated as a translation (unit Jacobian); L^P-norm invariance false without div A = 0
issues.why_classification: Two lemma statements are false at full generality and must be weakened or the scope restricted to divergence-free fields, and several proofs need their constants reworked: a contained, standard repair (Liouville/Gronwall estimate) that leaves every main theorem recognizably intact, hence more than a local wording fix but requiring no new proof architecture and causing no major loss.
